title: Chalet Hotels Ltd - 542399 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Chalet Q1 FY27 core revenue up 10% to INR5,140mn and EBITDA up 15% to INR2,400mn, with margin up 231bps to 46.7%.
summary.overview: Excluding residential, revenue grew 10% YoY to INR5,140mn and EBITDA rose 15% to INR2,400mn, with margin up 231bps to 46.7%; net profit was INR861mn. Hospitality RevPAR rose 6.5% on 8.5% ADR growth, with leisure resorts up 19% while FTA-dependent markets (Hyderabad, Bangalore) and MMR (Powai, Vashi) lagged. Commercial real estate revenue rose 18% to INR865mn with 85% margin, and the June 2026 rental run rate reached INR290mn per month. Management said August looks positive but declined to guide for the quarter given day-to-day volatility from the West Asia conflict.

financial_highlights.change: Slightly up vs March 2026 after acquisitions

segments.name: Hospitality
segments.commentary: Revenue INR4,185mn (+9%) and EBITDA INR1,784mn (+11%), margin 42.6%. Leisure portfolio RevPAR +19%; Pune high double-digit RevPAR growth; Hyderabad and Bangalore weak on occupancy due to FTA decline.

segments.name: Commercial real estate
segments.commentary: Revenue INR865mn (+18%) and EBITDA INR735mn (+21%). Portfolio committed about 91%; LOI signed for 66,000 sq ft more at Bangalore; monthly rental guided to INR300-320mn during FY27.

segments.name: Residential (Koramangala)
segments.commentary: Phase 1 completed; INR73mn revenue and INR31mn EBITDA recognised this quarter. 168 Phase 2 units to be handed over during FY27. Prior-year comparison distorted by one-time recognition.

segments.name: MMR portfolio
segments.commentary: Powai and Vashi (over 60% of MMR inventory) lagged on construction and renovation; JW Sahar saw good ADR growth with steady occupancy. MMR is about 43% of hospitality revenue in Q1.

guidance_outlook: Planned capex of about INR30bn over FY27-FY29 across hospitality and commercial real estate, largely funded by internal accruals.
Monthly rentals expected to scale to INR300-320mn during FY27; CIGNUS II Powai commissioning to drive step-change from FY28.
Taj Delhi Airport: minimum 70 rooms to launch in Q4 FY27, balance in phases within Q1 of next fiscal.
CIGNUS II Powai on track for substantial completion by FY27 end.
South Goa hotel construction expected to start by end of the current quarter, after the rainy season.
Management declined to guide for the quarter; August described as overall positive, September too far out.
capex_capacity: Hospitality portfolio to exceed 5,000 keys; management targets adding 500+ keys every year.
Added 129 keys at Bangalore; Dukes Retreat rebranded to Athiva with 67 additional keys.
Udaipur (Athiva) expansion awaiting approvals from local authorities and army cantonment; clarity expected in one to two quarters.
Mindspace projects at Hyderabad and Airoli have begun excavation; both on track.
CIGNUS II Powai adds 0.9mn sq ft of office space; INR10,914mn of net debt allocable to under-construction or yet-to-be-operational assets.
demand_pricing: Leisure resorts occupancy about 51% this quarter; management sees stabilised resort occupancy at 60-65%.
Athiva Khandala weekend rates sustained above INR15,000; weekday MICE demand still needs building.
Powai porch and Westin banquet connectivity due by quarter end; noisy construction to end in one to one and a half quarters.
FPS (Fairmont-adjacent MMR asset) renovation done at INR93 crore; rebranding to be announced in coming weeks.
Management said supply in MMR has been absorbed, with no major new supply expected in the next one to two years.
Commission rates paid to OTAs and GDS described as bottom-end of the market; OTA and transient mix fell but management said this is not a trend.

qa_highlights.question: Strategy for MMR underperformance, booking window, MICE, and competition including Fairmont near JW Marriott Sahar?
qa_highlights.answer: JW Sahar outperforming on ADR with steady occupancy; Powai under construction and FPS renovation driving near-term pain. Supply absorbed with no major supply in next one to two years.

qa_highlights.question: Will leisure reach 20% of portfolio target change, and Inder Residency expansion potential?
qa_highlights.answer: Strategy unchanged: leisure stays at about 20% of portfolio. Udaipur expansion awaiting two approvals; no firm number yet; existing building work proceeding.

qa_highlights.question: Timeline for resort occupancy to reach 70%+?
qa_highlights.answer: Resorts stabilise at 60-65%; Q1 was 51% and expected to keep improving. Athiva Khandala creating a premium MICE market.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 8.5% ADR growth from pricing or channel mix?
qa_highlights.answer: No major channel mix change; special corporate rates were raised slightly to retain them, and crew business increased.

qa_highlights.question: July trends and current outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Quarter started strongly, but visibility has worsened as the West Asia situation changes every 5 to 10 days. August looks positive; no quarterly guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Medium-term MMR occupancy ceiling, can it return to 77%+?
qa_highlights.answer: Management believes Powai and FPS can return to prior levels and go beyond. FPS was at about 140% fair share before refurbishment.

risks_watch: West Asia conflict: FTA arrivals stay flat; management said normalisation takes about 60 days after resolution, and sentiment has deteriorated again.
MMR: Powai and Vashi occupancy recovery depends on construction ending and the porch reopening in H2 FY27.
Bangalore relocation and group business softness; Hyderabad FTA exposure.
Leisure occupancy may be partly driven by domestic shift from outbound travel; management says the 60-65% target is a given but timing is uncertain.
Goa and Udaipur project timelines depend on local and army approvals.
Net debt rising with acquisitions; INR10.9bn tied to assets not yet operational.
summary.management_tone: Confident on domestic and leisure demand and long-term Powai and resort upside, but cautious on the near term. Management repeatedly declined to give quarterly guidance or precise timelines, citing day-to-day volatility from the West Asia conflict and pending approvals.
